verses.text: Naaman was the commander of the army of the king of Syria. His master thought very highly of him and respected him, because through Naaman the LORD had given Syria victory. He was a brave soldier, but he had a skin disease called leprosy.
Raiding parties from Syria had gone into Israel and taken a young girl captive. She became a servant to Naaman's wife.
She said to her mistress, "If only my master would go to the prophet in Samaria! He would heal him of his leprosy."
Naaman went and told his master the king what the girl from Israel had said.

The king of Syria said, "Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So Naaman left. He took with him about three hundred and forty kilograms of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten sets of clothes.
He took the letter to the king of Israel. It said, "With this letter I am sending my servant Naaman to you, so that you can heal him of his leprosy."

When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God? Can I kill and bring back to life? Why does this man send someone to me to be healed of leprosy? You can see he is trying to pick a fight with me!"

When Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent him this message: "Why have you torn your clothes? Send the man to me, and he will know there is a prophet in Israel."
So Naaman went with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
Elisha sent a messenger out to say to him, "Go and wash yourself seven times in the Jordan River. Your skin will be healed, and you will be clean."
But Naaman became angry and went away. He said, "I thought he would surely come out to me, stand there, call on the name of the LORD his God, wave his hand over the sore spot, and heal my leprosy.
Aren't the Abana and Pharpar rivers in Damascus better than any of the waters in Israel? Couldn't I wash in them and be clean?" So he turned and stormed off in a rage.
But his servants came to him and said, "Father, if the prophet had told you to do something hard, wouldn't you have done it? So why not do it when he simply tells you, 'Wash and be clean'?"
So Naaman went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, as the man of God had told him. His skin became healthy, like the skin of a young child, and he was clean.

Then Naaman and all his men went back to the man of God. He stood in front of Elisha and said, "Now I know that there is no God in all the world except in Israel. So please accept a gift from your servant."
But Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives, the God I serve, I will not accept anything." Naaman kept urging him to take it, but he refused.

Naaman said, "If you will not, then please let me, your servant, take home as much soil as two mules can carry. From now on, your servant will never again offer a burnt offering or sacrifice to any other god except the LORD.

But may the LORD forgive your servant for one thing. When my master goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship, he leans on my arm, and I have to bow down there too. When I bow down in the temple of Rimmon, may the LORD forgive your servant for this."
Elisha said to him, "Go in peace." So Naaman left and went a short distance.

Then Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, thought, "My master let this Syrian, Naaman, off too easily by not accepting what he brought. As surely as the LORD lives, I will run after him and get something from him."
So Gehazi hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw someone running after him, he got down from his chariot to meet him and asked, "Is everything all right?"

Gehazi answered, "Everything is all right. My master sent me to say, 'Two young men from the group of prophets have just come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them thirty-four kilograms of silver and two sets of clothes.'"

Naaman said, "Please, take sixty-eight kilograms." He kept urging Gehazi to take it. He tied up the silver in two bags, with two sets of clothes, and gave them to two of his servants, who carried them ahead of Gehazi.
When Gehazi came to the hill, he took the things from the servants and hid them in the house. Then he sent the men away, and they left.
Then Gehazi went in and stood before his master. Elisha asked him, "Where have you been, Gehazi?" He answered, "Your servant did not go anywhere."

But Elisha said to him, "Was my spirit not with you when the man got down from his chariot to meet you? Is this the time to take money and clothes, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and cattle, and male and female servants?
Now Naaman's leprosy will cling to you and to your descendants forever." When Gehazi left Elisha, his skin had leprosy. It was as white as snow.
